chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:
Archery (throwing of arrows) is one of the arrows of Islam.

key_terms.سِهَامِ الْإِسْلَامِ: Arrows of Islam (metaphor for fundamental practices)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of archery in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi elevates archery beyond mere physical skill, framing it as a spiritual discipline and a form of jihad that strengthens the Muslim community's readiness for defense. The metaphor of the 'arrow' underscores the precision and intent required in both martial practice and spiritual conduct, linking physical training directly to religious merit.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Talha Bin Zayd, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The throwing of arrows (archery) is from the arrows of Al-Islam’.
en.sarwar: 10. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa‘dan from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the angels do not attend anything except (horse racing) contest and man’s playing with his wife.”
